name: bc_program_call
prose: Static function bc_program_call(p, code, bgn) in bc/src/program.c (starting line 1787), returns nothing; it executes a function-call instruction. It reads the number of arguments nargs and the function index from the bytecode at *bgn, sets the new instruction pointer to index 0 of that function and looks the function up in p->fns. Errors are raised with bc_verr/bc_err and do not return: BC_ERR_EXEC_UNDEF_FUNC when the function has no code, BC_ERR_EXEC_PARAMS when nargs differs from the function's parameter count, and BC_ERR_EXEC_VOID_VAL (bc_err) in the argument loop when an argument is a void result. It records the current length of the results stack in the new frame (so the callee's results can be discarded later), then for each argument it copies the result into a variable with bc_program_copyToVar, which pops that argument result from the results stack (the arguments do not stay on the stack); parameters not passed are initialized as empty or default variables, and the instruction pointer of the callee is pushed on the instruction stack. The results stack depth is checked only by an assert, not at run time.
note: Reviewer round 15 (results-stack check is only an assert) right (program.c); the old prose said the arguments stay on the results stack, which is wrong because copyToVar pops each one. Tally 1 right 0 wrong. I read the whole function.

name: bc_program_reset
prose: Function bc_program_reset(p) in bc/src/program.c (starting line 3003), returns nothing. It resets the interpreter after an error or interrupt: it pops the instruction stack down to the bottom frame, resets the bottom frame's instruction index to the end of its function (so execution stops), clears the tail-call and related state, and clears the signal flag. In interactive dc mode (not bc) it also pops the results stack down to its bottom, by npop, popping the top nresults entries (not just one), so the results stack ends up with the entries that existed before the failed command removed. It does not return a status.
note: Both reviewers (original and round 15, about popping the top nresults entries in interactive dc) right. Tally 2 right 0 wrong. The description is qualified: I read the function but did not trace every state field it clears.

name: br_eax_aad_inject
prose: Function br_eax_aad_inject(ctx, data, len) in bearssl/src/aead/eax.c (starting line 267), returns nothing. It feeds additional authenticated data into the CBC-MAC part of the EAX state for the current phase. Full blocks are passed to do_cbcmac_chunk. For a partial pending block it copies bytes into the buffer; in the branch that completes a 16-byte block it does not set ctx->ptr to 16 before calling do_cbcmac_chunk, whose entry expects ptr to be 0 or 16, so as read from the source the completed block appears not to be MACed and may be overwritten (state as observed from reading, not run).
note: Old prose had no check of the ptr handling. No reviewer claim. This is a reading of the source, not an execution, so it is stated as how the code reads. Tally 0 right 0 wrong.

name: br_eax_run
prose: Static function br_eax_run(ctx, data, len, encrypt) in bearssl/src/aead/eax.c (starting line 336), returns nothing. With len == 0 it returns immediately. It first finishes any partial block: it XORs the buffered bytes with the keystream, and the pending block is passed to the MAC when it completes. It then processes bulk data with CTR and CBC-MAC together; the last 1 to 16 bytes are held in the buffer rather than MACed, and ctx->ptr is set accordingly.

name: br_pem_decoder_run
prose: Function br_pem_decoder_run(ctx, data, len) in bearssl/src/codec/pemdec.c (lines 223-526, the T0 generated interpreter, not t0_run), returns size_t, the number of input bytes consumed. It runs the compiled T0 PEM decoder: a loop over opcodes 0-28 plus the T0_ENTER opcode for word calls, using the CTX macro for the decoder state; there are no bounds checks on the T0 stacks. It consumes input until it must report an event (begin/end of an object, data chunk, error) or the data is exhausted, and returns the consumed count.

name: mul20
prose: Static function mul20(d, a, b) in bearssl/src/ec/ec_c25519_m15.c, returns nothing; it multiplies two 20-limb numbers with 13-bit limbs into a 40-limb result d. There are two variants. Under BR_SLOW_MUL15 a Karatsuba version computes the product and finishes with norm13(d, w, 40) followed by d[39] += cc << 13; the fast variant computes the columns and sets d[39] = norm13(d, t, 39). Input limbs are expected to be 13-bit values; d may overlap a or b. For valid inputs the final carry into d[39] is 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 (d[39] carry) mixed: it is zero for valid inputs but the slow variant does add cc << 13 to d[39]. Tally 0 right 0 wrong, 1 mixed.

name: square20
prose: Static function square20(d, a) in bearssl/src/ec/ec_c25519_m15.c, returns nothing; it squares a 20-limb number with 13-bit limbs into 40 limbs. Under BR_SLOW_MUL15 it simply calls mul20(d, a, a); the fast variant computes the squares and doubled cross products directly and ends with the same normalization (d[39] receives the final carry via norm13). Inputs are 13-bit limbs and d may overlap a.
note: Reviewer round 15 mixed, as for mul20. Tally 0 right 0 wrong, 1 mixed.

name: p256_add_mixed
prose: Static function p256_add_mixed(P1, P2) in bearssl/src/ec/ec_p256_m15.c (starting line 1593), returns uint32_t. It adds the affine point P2 (z2 implicitly 1, so z2 is ignored) to the Jacobian point P1 and always overwrites P1 with x3, y3 and z3 = h * z1. It returns 1 if r = y2 * z1^3 - y1 is nonzero modulo p, and 0 otherwise.
note: Reviewer round 15 right (return value is whether r is nonzero). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: br_rsa_i15_compute_privexp
prose: Function br_rsa_i15_compute_privexp(d, sk, e) in bearssl/src/rsa/rsa_i15_privexp.c (lines 29-320), with d a void pointer, sk a br_rsa_private_key and e a uint32_t scalar public exponent; returns size_t. It returns 0 if e < 3 or e is even, or if p or q has a bit length outside the supported range (the byte length must be 5 up to BR_MAX_RSA_FACTOR/8) or is even. If d is NULL it returns dlen = (n_bitlen + 7) >> 3 without computing. It computes phi = (p-1)(q-1) = k * e + r; r == 0 returns 0. Using a 62-iteration binary GCD it finds the inverse; if the result a is not 1 it returns 0. It then computes d = u0 + v0 * k, encodes it big-endian into d and returns dlen.
note: Reviewer round 15 (e is a scalar, not a big integer, and there is no cc parameter) right; the old prose treated e and phi as big integers. Tally 1 right 0 wrong. The whole function was read.

name: br_rsa_i31_compute_privexp
prose: Function br_rsa_i31_compute_privexp(d, sk, e) in bearssl/src/rsa/rsa_i31_privexp.c (lines 29-318), same algorithm as the i15 version but with 31-bit limbs; returns size_t. It returns 0 for e < 3 or even e, for even or out-of-range p or q lengths, when r = phi mod e is 0, or when the final gcd is not 1; with d NULL it returns the encoded length (n_bitlen + 7) >> 3; otherwise it writes the big-endian d and returns that length.

name: process
prose: Static function process(bl_t bl) in blacklistd/blacklistd.c (lines 171-282), returns nothing. It receives and handles one message. If clock_gettime or bl_recv fails it logs and returns early without closing anything. It then goes to out (which closes bi->bi_fd and logs under debug) when getremoteaddress fails, when no rule matches ("no rule matched"), when state_get returns -1, when run_change returns -1 (nothing logged inside process), and for BL_DELETE when last == 0 (no log). BL_ABUSE sets the count to nfail - 1 and then acts like BL_ADD; BL_BADUSER writes the state back unchanged; any unknown type logs LOG_ERR "unknown message" and still calls state_put.

name: bl_send
prose: Function bl_send(b, e, rfd, cred, fd, ...) in blocklist/old/old_bl.c (lines 370-431), returns int. It tries sendmsg up to 6 times (NTRIES): bl_init before each attempt, bl_reset after failures 1 to 5. If bl_getsock fails it returns -1 with errno EINVAL. A success on the 6th attempt still returns -1 because the final test is tried >= NTRIES, not the sendmsg result.

name: bl_recv
prose: Function bl_recv(b) in blocklist/old/old_bl.c (lines 433-554), returns a pointer to the internal b_info, or NULL. recvmsg failure returns NULL. It walks the control messages: an SCM_RIGHTS message of bad length closes the received fds; a missing fd or missing credentials returns NULL; a received fd is not closed on later errors. A short message or version mismatch returns NULL. Otherwise it fills bi and returns the internal b_info.

name: pcloseve
prose: Function pcloseve(FILE *iop) in libc popenve.c (lines 238-279), returns int. It takes pidlist_lock itself (in _REENTRANT builds); if iop is not in the list it sets errno ESRCH and returns -1. It then fcloses the stream, unlinks the entry, waits with waitpid retrying on EINTR, frees the entry, and returns -1 on waitpid error or the wait status otherwise.

prose: Function sockaddr_snprintf(buf, len, fmt, sa) in port/sockaddr_snprintf.c (lines 165-385), returns int. The initial getnameinfo with NI_NUMERICHOST failure returns -1; failures of later %A/%P lookups are ignored. The ADDC macro counts characters even past the end of the buffer; the output is NUL-terminated and the return value is the number of characters produced.
